additions.reason: The Torah explicitly invokes 'נֶפֶשׁ חַיָה הוּא שְׁמוֹ' (Genesis 2:19 as interpreted by the Talmud — Yerushalmi Taanit ch. 2) to establish that the Name of God = life-force. 'Living soul' (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה) is thus a bechina of both שם (the Name) and חיות (life-force). The proof text reads: 'וְהַשֵּׁם הוּא הַחִיּוּת, בִּבְחִינַת: נֶפֶשׁ חַיָה הוּא שְׁמוֹ' — the Name is the life-force, in the aspect of: a living soul — that is His Name. This forms an explicit bechina triangle: שם ↔ חיות ↔ נפש חיה.
additions.source_quote: וְהַשֵּׁם הוּא הַחִיּוּת, בִּבְחִינַת: נֶפֶשׁ חַיָה הוּא שְׁמוֹ

additions.reason: The Torah states that people call the day after Yom Kippur 'שֵׁם ה'' — 'the Name of God.' This is bechina language: מָחֳרַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים is called שֵׁם ה', placing it in the same domain as שם, שבת, and שמא דקדשא בריך הוא. The dataset records the related edge (יום הכפורים → נתגלה בחינת שם ה) as type 'cause', which captures the causal dimension. But the NAMING of the day as 'שם ה'' is a bechina: the day itself embodies the revealed Name. This node should be added to Package 1 as an additional expression of the Divine Name being present and accessible.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה שֶׁקּוֹרִין הָעוֹלָם אֶת מָחֳרַת יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שֵׁם ה'

additions.reason: The verse 'צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם' (Proverbs 10:25) is quoted as the explicit scriptural basis for identifying the Tzaddik as the Simple Foundation. The text states: 'בְּחִינַת הַצַּדִּיק, בְּחִינַת: צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם' — the verse IS the bechina name for what the Tzaddik is. This phrase functions as a distinct concept node that explicitly bridges the Tzaddik and the יסוד עולם (foundation of the world). It belongs in Package 2 as the scriptural formulation of the Tzaddik = יסוד הפשוט equation.

מחרת יום הכפורים — The day after Yom Kippur is called 'שם ה'' — bechina language in the source text; dataset captures only the causal relationship
צדיק יסוד עולם — The scriptural verse used to name the Tzaddik as the world's foundation; cited multiple times with bechina language
ארבעה יסודות (אש, רוח, מים, עפר) — The four elements: correctly ABSENT from bechina dataset because their relationship to the Tzaddik is eitza (they flow FROM him, they are not the same thing as him)
מידות — Character traits: flow from the four elements → correctly absent (eitza, not bechina)

שמו משותף בשמנו — 'His Name is shared with ours': this phrase expresses the bechina between God's Name and the names of Israel, but is used in the text as an explanatory bridge, not as a standalone concept node
analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: Package 1 (שם/חיות = Divine life-force) mirrors Package 3 (ענשים/מיתה = death/severance from that life-force). The Torah's central argument is that punishment severs the connection to the Name/life-force, and since God's Name is shared with ours, punishment to Israel affects God Himself. The evil mirror is structurally inverted: where Package 1 is the Name as the source of life, Package 3 is punishment as the cutting off from that source.
